MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  JULY 15, 2019

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 6:08 p.m. at Highridge Park, 29035 Highridge Rd, Rolling Hills Estates,
  California by CHAIR RETZ.

  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR RETZ led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Retz, Persichina, McCormick, Romanelli, Ciarolla,
  Bain, Pope

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  None

  STAFF PRESENT:  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  Michael Goldsmith, Maintenance Superintendent
  Cynthia Morquecho, Comm. Services Supervisor
  Daniel A-Haja, Comm. Services Coordinator

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF JUNE 17, 2019

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF JUNE
  17, 2019.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  None

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  WALL OF RECOGNITION PLAQUES

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO provided a brief overview per
  the agenda material.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
JULY 15, 2019
   CHAIR RETZ asked if staff would install the plaques, which was affirmed.  Asked for a
  roll call on the matter. All commissioners said yes to the plaques.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK to:

  RECOMMEND TO THE CITY COUNCIL TO APPROVE THE ADDITION OF
  BRONZE PLAQUES HONORING DOUGLAS PRICHARD’S AND ANDY CLARK’S
  TENURE WITH THE CITY.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  B.  SILVER SPUR LITTLE LEAGUE REQUEST TO PLACE SCORE KEEPERS
  SHED AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK SPORTS FIELD

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS provided an overview

  CHAIR RETZ recommends that the Silver Spur come to the Park & Activities Commission
  for permission before placing any structures in parks.

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA stated that a meeting was held at Fred Hesse Park in
  November 2018 with COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, COMMUNITY SERVICES
  DIRECTOR, ANDY CLARK and COMMUNITY SERVICES COORDIANTOR, DANIEL A-
  HAJA, and Peter Cho, Mike Shull, Matt Bates, and Adam Brown of Silver Spur Little
  League informing the League that they must seek prior approval by the City before any
  new structures are placed at the park.

  CHAIR RETZ and COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted that the Little League seemed to
  have violated the agreement with full knowledge of the City’s expectations prior to the
  violation.

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA noted that other organizations have asked to place structures
  in parks but were denied unless no other storage options were available and as a matter
  of policy the Commission does not recommend other organizations to place structures of
  any kind. VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA additionally noted that historically for Pony League
  and Silver Spur Little League has used a bench scorekeepers and he did not see the need
  for a structure

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted in his records that the meeting between the City
  and Silver Spur Little League occurred Tuesday November 13, 2018. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI stated that at that meeting they reviewed the existing Agreement between
  the City and the Silver Spur Little League, expectations from the League and the City,
  upgrades to electrical outlets, drinking fountains being moved, and how to control
  grooming of the outfields and infields. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI suggests the Little
  League remove the shed and then appeal to the Park and Activities Commission.

  SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH added the expected relocation of the drinking fountain
  is in the location of the current scorekeeper shed.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
JULY 15, 2019
   CHAIR RETZ and COMMISSSIONER BAIN made the recommendation that the structure
  be removed.

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA stated the Silver Spur League already has a score keeping
  bench and needs only one scorekeeper which is feasible for games at the park. He has
  also questioned if the proposed structure was ADA compliant.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN stated that Silver Spur Little League could bring up any changes
  or improvements at the time of their agreement renewal.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS noted City Staff will be responsible for notifying
  Silver Spur Little League to remove the structure. There may also be a mechanism for
  penalty in City Code if Silver Spur Little League does not comply. ASSISTANT CITY
  MANAGER DAVIS suggested a time period of 15 days to allow for removal of structure
  since the Little League received initial notice from the City after the June Commission
  meeting when the structure was noted to have been placed.

  CHAIR RETZ agreed that 15 days from the date of notice to remove the structure was
  reasonable given the prior notice.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted the rationale for the notice was that the agreement
  was not followed when installing the structure.

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to:

  TO NOTIFY SILVER SPUR LITTLE LEAGUE TO REMOVE THE UNPERMITTED
  STRUCTURE WITHIN 15 DAYS AND DENY THE REQUEST FOR FUTURE
  PLACEMENT OF THE SCORE KEEPERS SHED AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK
  BALL FIELD

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  C.  CALIFORNIA DESPERADOS AND COWBOY MOUNTED SHOOTING
  ASSOCIATION - MOUNTED SHOOTING COMPETITION EVENT AT ERNIE
  HOWLETT PARK

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO provided an overview per the
  agenda material.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER ALEXA DAVIS clarified that after receiving the request in
  July and to accommodate the proposed event date, staff proceed to seek the Commission
  approval first with the Equestrian Committee’s input at its next meeting for final approval
  by City Council.

  CHAIR RETZ stated that firing blanks can still pose a safety issue that he is concerned
  about having in a public park area.

  AUDIENCE MEMBER VICKI SHINN, 23 Roanwood, expressed concern that the horse
  show would take away from local horse shows and its community and would adversely

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
JULY 15, 2019
   impact the arena. MAINTENANCE SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH confirmed that
  there would be no impact to arena as a result of this activity.

  AUDIENCE MEMBER CARRIE SILVANO stated concern about notifications not providing
  a good warning and that the event does not seem to be a community event for Rolling
  Hills Estates. She further stated that she is concerned about the repeated sound of gunfire.
  AUDIENCE MEMBER VICKI SHINN added that the entire equestrian facility should be
  closed and the sound of gunfire could also impact tennis players. She further expressed
  that event poses a safety issue and a disruption to the maintenance of the rings. She read
  aloud a letter from Debbie Taymore, 47 Buckskin, opposing the event on the grounds of
  safety and municipal code concerns.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS expressed that the City Attorney addressed the
  municipal code and explained that this event would be comparable to a film shoot where
  no firearms with bullets are actually used.

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted that the event has taken
  placed in the Tejon Pass area but organizers were looking for a cooler region to hold the
  event.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER ALEXA DAVIS noted that the activity was a held as a
  demonstration at the City Celebration around the year of 2008 at the Empty Saddle Club,
  coordinated by Dale Allen.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN questioned how many competitors participate in the event;
  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR responded with 25 participants.

  AUDIENCE MEMBER PAM SCHACTER stated that the Portuguese Bend Horse Show
  should be notified since the proposed date is close to their event date and that she notified
  the greater equestrian community.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted that the proponents of the event should be heard
  and invited to the Equestrian Committee meeting.

  CHAIR RETZ noted that the request came in late and stated concern about the time to
  review thoroughly with the Equestrian Committee’s review and input.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA to:

  NOT APPROVE THE EVENT BUT SEND THE ITEM TO THE EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE FOR THEIR REVIEW AND INPUT AND RETURN TO THE PARK &
  ACTIVITIES COMMISSION FOR FURTHER CONSIDERATION.

  The motion carried without objection.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
JULY 15, 2019
   D.  MASTER STREET TREE LIST REVIEW

  SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH provided an overview per the agenda material.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if the Chinese Elm would still be on the list of
  approved trees and if the resident who requested the tree will be notified.

  SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH confirmed the Chinese Elm will not be on the list and
  that the resident will be notified with a finalized tree list.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to:

  ACCEPT STAFF RECOMMENDATION TO UPDATE MASTER STREET TREE
  LIST BY REMOVING THE EVERGREEN PEAR AND TWO EUCALYPTUS
  VARIETIES, FLAMING AND RED IRON BARK.

  The motion carried without objection.

  8.  ADJOURN TO THE PEPPERTREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD MEETING

  CHAIR RETZ made a motion

  ADOURN TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD MEETING

  A.  HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE SUBCOMMITTEE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMUNITY SERVICES COORDINATOR DANIEL A-HAJA stated registration numbers
  are on par with last year’s numbers and sponsorships are growing through contractor,
  Michael Hogue.

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA asked what the last day would be to find out if the route
  needed to use an alternate route due to the CalWater project along Rolling Hills Road.
  COMMUNITY SERVICES COORDINATOR AHAJA responded that it would be confirmed
  by August 1 and that an alternate route has been identified through the usage of the bridle
  trail across the street and that traffic would be controlled by two Sheriff’s Posse mounted
  patrols on either side of the road.

  B.  TRACY AUSTIN DOUBLES TOURNAMENT UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMUNITY SERVICES COORDINATOR AHAJA reported that registration numbers
  are on par with last year’s numbers and sponsorships are growing with the addition of
  local grocery stores. An increase in sponsor booths and teams have also been noted.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS expressed that a conflicting Juniors tournament in
  Irvine is taking place the same weekend as the tournament. She also confirmed the
  Commission volunteer assignments for the weekend.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
JULY 15, 2019
   9.  RECONVENE TO PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING

  CHAIR RETZ made a motion,

  RECONVENE TO THE PARK AND ACITIVITIES COMMITTEE MEETING

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  10.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted no new reports or
  updates were received by Commissioners.

  B.  CITY CELEBRATION SUBCOMMITTEE UPDATE VERBAL REPORT

  No report.

  11.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH provided a brief report per the last park tour at Ernie
  Howlett Park the drinking fountain and trees by the barns have been addressed, the chain-
  link fence in the back near baseball field and a main line leak have been repaired.

  B.  NATURE CENTER STUDY UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS noted the final study went to the City Council in
  June and that a City Council subcommittee was formed to meet with the architect to
  consider an alternate proposal that would reduce cost.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI added that there was no exact budget given to the Park
  & Activities Commission in advance and expressed disappointment in the process. He
  stated that it would be helpful to incorporate cost early in the discussion of the project and
  have better defined parameters.

  12.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL MEETING ACTION MEMO OF JUNE 25, 2019

  Received and filed

  B.  CITY COUNCIL MEETING ACTION MEMO OF JULY 8, 2019

  Received and filed

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
JULY 15, 2019
   13.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  TABOR GROVE PROJECT UPDATE

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted that more input was
  needed from the neighborhood.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS explained that staff plans to coordinate a
  neighborhood meeting and then coming back to the Commission with their input.

  CHAIR RETZ noted the past history of the Grove project and mentioned the Commission
  received five letters of disapproval from the local HOA with over 100 members. More
  information would be needed to see if the HOA is on board with the project.

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS explained that it appeared the neighborhood was
  in support of the project initially, but then faced opposition with the expanded scope of the
  project, which includes the scenic corridor. The next step would be to clarify the next
  phases of the project and then charge and encroachment fee after the full scope of the
  two phases have been approved.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN suggested that the Commission see what is brought to the HOA
  before it is sent back to the neighborhood for review and approval, and that a Commission
  Member be present during the meeting.

  B.  VETERAN'S MEMORIAL DONATION

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted that staff received a
  request to establish a Veteran’s Memorial and possible donation of funds to support the
  project. Staff will return with more detail at a future meeting for Commission consideration.

  C.  PARK DEVELOPMENT TIMELINE

  It was reported that staff is working on a timeline of park updates and will return to the
  Commission at a future date with more information.

  D.  BUTCHER PARK UPDATE

  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS noted that more information was need from
  Metropolitan Water District (MWD) for a concise timeline.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if the funds from MWD for the reservoir were still
  available. ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER DAVIS stated that the funds will be available but
  the amount and timeline of allocation is still unknown.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
JULY 15, 2019
   14.  PARK TOURS

  The Park and Activities Commission toured Highridge Park and noted the following:

  •  Bathroom and bulletin boards were reported to get updated, washed and
  refurbished this month
  •  Staff needs a key to the locked softball shed
  •  Drainage pipes from nearby residential homes are being led onto the park trails
  •  Park course station had exposed bolts
  •  Broken fence rails noted
  •  Wood rot on some posts near the entrance of the park due to heavy watering from
  sprinklers.

  15.  ADJOURNMENT

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK
  to,

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 7:16 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES MEETING ON AUGUST 19, 2019 AT 6:00 P.M., WHICH WILL MEET
  AT CHANDLER PRESERVE, 95 BUCKSKIN LN., ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  _____________________________
  Daniel A-Haja  Cynthia Morquecho
  Community Services Coordinator  Community Services Supervisor

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  8
JULY 15, 2019
